title: The Running Chicken Nebula
caption: The Running Chicken Nebula, imaged by ESO's VLT Survey Telescope
celestial: IC 2944, Running Chicken Nebula · constellation Centaurus · about 6500 light-years away (source figure)

recognition.text: Official ESO press-release image. No published audience rating.

story: Wispy pink plumes of gas and dust fill this vast image of the Running Chicken Nebula, known to astronomers as IC 2944. The nebula is made up of several separate clouds, and the VLT Survey Telescope, hosted at ESO's Paranal site, captured all of them.

The pink clouds glow because young, hot stars within them are lighting them up. This kind of nebula is an H II region, made of hydrogen gas that shines after being energized by the intense light of newborn stars. Gas and dust are mixed together throughout these clouds.

The image itself is enormous. It contains 1.5 billion pixels and covers an area of sky about as large as 25 full Moons. Survey telescopes like the VST are built to capture wide stretches of sky in fine detail, so a single picture can show an entire nebula along with its surroundings.
scale: Using the source's listed field of view (149.99 x 131.99 arcminutes) and distance (6500 light years), the frame spans roughly 284 × 250 light-years. Its light set out about 6,500 years before reaching the telescope.

understand.summary: This visible-light image was taken with the OmegaCAM camera on ESO's VLT Survey Telescope, through u, g, r and i filters plus a hydrogen-alpha filter. The color assigned to each filter is not published.
filters: 350 nm · Optical u (VLT Survey Telescope OmegaCAM)
480 nm · Optical g (VLT Survey Telescope OmegaCAM)
625 nm · Optical r (VLT Survey Telescope OmegaCAM)
659 nm · Optical H-alpha (VLT Survey Telescope OmegaCAM)
770 nm · Optical i (VLT Survey Telescope OmegaCAM)
understand.eye: The long exposures and the hydrogen-alpha filter bring out faint glowing gas that would be very hard to see by eye.
